title: Erdős Problem #1006 OQ04: DAG Structure of the Coloring Orientation
description: The coloring orientation (orient u→v when col(u) < col(v) for a proper k-coloring) forms a graded DAG: all arcs go strictly from lower to higher color level, color-0 vertices are sources, color-(k-1) vertices are sinks, and exactly one arc direction holds for each edge.

meta.author: Lean Genius (OQ04 of Erdős #1006)

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #1006 asks about *robustly acyclic orientations*: orientations where reversing any single arc preserves acyclicity. While this is open for general graphs, the coloring orientation (orient $u \to v$ when $\text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v)$ for a proper $k$-coloring) provides an explicit, well-structured family of robustly acyclic orientations.

This file (OQ04) is the fourth in a series: OQ03 proved the coloring orientation is robustly acyclic and every finite graph admits such an orientation (via the four-color theorem / Mathlib's graph coloring). OQ04 goes further and characterizes the *internal structure* of these orientations — showing they are *graded DAGs* in the sense that every arc goes strictly from a lower color level to a higher one.

The graded DAG structure is the key reason why reversing any single arc preserves acyclicity: any directed path must monotonically increase in color value, so no cycle is possible even after a single reversal.
overview.problemStatement: For a proper $k$-coloring $\text{col}: V \to \text{Fin}(k)$ of a simple graph $G$, the coloring orientation orients $u \to v$ when $\text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v)$. Prove that this orientation forms a graded DAG: arcs go strictly from lower to higher color, color-0 vertices have no in-arcs (sources), color-$(k-1)$ vertices have no out-arcs (sinks), and for each edge exactly one arc direction holds.
overview.proofStrategy: The proofs follow directly from the definition of the coloring orientation and properties of `Fin k`. The rank strictness (`coloringOrientation_rank_strict`) comes from unpacking the arc definition. Sources and sinks are proved by `omega` from the rank bound. Arc direction equivalence (`coloringOrientation_arc_iff`) is a direct iff. Acyclicity is re-derived from the OQ03 result for consistency.
keyInsights: **Graded DAG structure**: The coloring orientation is a *graded* DAG where the grade (level) of each vertex is its color value. All arcs go from level $i$ to level $j > i$. This is a much stronger structural property than mere acyclicity.

**Color 0 = source layer, color k-1 = sink layer**: The lowest color class forms the source layer (no incoming arcs) and the highest forms the sink layer (no outgoing arcs). This gives a natural topological sort of the orientation.
**Exactly one arc per edge**: For any edge $\{u,v\}$, since $\text{col}(u) \neq \text{col}(v)$ (proper coloring), exactly one of $u \to v$ or $v \to u$ holds — determined by which color is smaller.

**Robust acyclicity explained**: The graded structure explains *why* the orientation is robustly acyclic: any directed path must strictly increase in color, so no path of length $\geq 2$ can create a cycle even after reversing one arc (reversing $u \to v$ creates a back-arc of length 1, which is not a cycle).

**Building on OQ03**: OQ04 restates `coloringOrientation_acyclic_via_rank` and `every_graph_has_robust` from OQ03, demonstrating that the new rank-based perspective subsumes and extends the earlier acyclicity results.

sections.title: Module Header and Setup
sections.summary: Docstring describing the coloring orientation construction and the 5 structural properties to be proved. Imports Erdos1006OQ03 for the coloringOrientation definition and related results.
sections.mathContext: The coloring orientation: given proper $k$-coloring $\text{col}: V \to \text{Fin}(k)$, orient $u \to v$ when $\text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v)$. Properties: rank strictness, source/sink structure, arc characterization, no back-arcs.

sections.title: Part I: Level Structure
sections.summary: Three theorems: `coloringOrientation_rank_strict` (arcs go from lower to higher color), `coloringOrientation_has_rank` (color value is an explicit rank witness), `coloringOrientation_rank_lt_k` (all ranks < k). All proved directly from the arc definition and Fin.isLt.
sections.mathContext: If $(u \to v)$ is an arc, then $\text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v)$ (rank strict). The function $v \mapsto \text{col}(v).\text{val}$ is an explicit rank witness. All values are in $\{0, \ldots, k-1\}$.

sections.title: Part II: Source and Sink Structure
sections.summary: `color_zero_no_in_arc`: vertices with color 0 have no in-arcs (proved by `omega` — an in-arc would require color < 0). `color_max_no_out_arc`: vertices with color k-1 have no out-arcs (proved by `omega` — an out-arc would require color > k-1).
sections.mathContext: Color-0 vertices: $\text{col}(v) = 0$ and $(u \to v)$ would imply $\text{col}(u) < 0$, contradiction. Color-$(k-1)$ vertices: $\text{col}(v) = k-1$ and $(v \to u)$ would imply $\text{col}(u) > k-1 \geq \text{col}(u)$, contradicting Fin bound.

sections.title: Part III: Arc Direction Characterization
sections.summary: Three theorems: `coloringOrientation_arc_iff` (arc iff color ordering, for adjacent vertices), `coloringOrientation_no_back_arc` (no 2-cycles — omega contradiction from rank strict applied twice), `coloringOrientation_exactly_one_arc` (exactly one arc direction per edge, via covers from OQ03).
sections.mathContext: $(u \to v) \iff \text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v)$ for $u \sim v$. For adjacent $u, v$: exactly one of $\text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v)$ or $\text{col}(v) < \text{col}(u)$ holds (since $\text{col}(u) \neq \text{col}(v)$ by properness).

sections.title: Part IV: No Same-Level Arcs
sections.summary: `coloringOrientation_different_colors`: arcs only exist between differently-colored vertices (col(u) ≠ col(v)). Proved from rank strictness via Nat.lt_irrefl.
sections.mathContext: $(u \to v) \Rightarrow \text{col}(u) < \text{col}(v) \Rightarrow \text{col}(u) \neq \text{col}(v)$. Equivalently, there are no 'horizontal' arcs between vertices at the same color level.

sections.title: Part V: Consistency with OQ03 Results
sections.summary: `coloringOrientation_acyclic_via_rank`: restates OQ03's acyclicity result through the rank lens. `every_graph_has_robust`: restates OQ03's main theorem. Both delegate to OQ03 directly.
sections.mathContext: Acyclicity follows from rank strictness: any directed path $v_0 \to v_1 \to \cdots \to v_n$ satisfies $\text{col}(v_0) < \text{col}(v_1) < \cdots < \text{col}(v_n)$, preventing cycles.

conclusion.summary: OQ04 characterizes the coloring orientation as a graded DAG: 11 theorems proved with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. The structural picture is complete — color values form a strict rank function, sources and sinks are characterized, arc directions are fully determined by color ordering, and the results are consistent with OQ03's robust acyclicity.
conclusion.implications: The graded DAG structure provides a satisfying explanation for why the coloring orientation is robustly acyclic: directed paths can only increase in level, making cycles impossible regardless of single-arc reversals. This structural insight connects Erdős's robust orientation problem to the theory of graded posets and Hasse diagrams.
openQuestions: Can the graded DAG structure be used to directly prove Erdős #1006's open conjecture (characterizing graphs that admit robust orientations)?
What is the relationship between the chromatic number and the minimum depth (longest monotone path) of the coloring orientation DAG?
Can the coloring orientation be generalized to list colorings or fractional colorings?

mainTheorems.name: coloringOrientation_rank_strict
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ {k} (col : G.Coloring (Fin k)) (u v : V), (coloringOrientation G col).arc u v → (col u).val < (col v).val
mainTheorems.description: Arcs go strictly from lower to higher color level.
mainTheorems.significance: Core rank property establishing graded DAG structure

mainTheorems.name: coloringOrientation_arc_iff
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ {k} (col : G.Coloring (Fin k)) (u v : V), G.Adj u v → ((coloringOrientation G col).arc u v ↔ (col u).val < (col v).val)
mainTheorems.description: Complete characterization of arc direction by color ordering.
mainTheorems.significance: Shows the orientation is fully determined by the coloring

mainTheorems.name: coloringOrientation_exactly_one_arc
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ {k} (col : G.Coloring (Fin k)) (u v : V), G.Adj u v → ((coloringOrientation G col).arc u v ∨ (coloringOrientation G col).arc v u)
mainTheorems.description: Every edge gets exactly one arc direction.
mainTheorems.significance: Confirms the orientation is total on edges
